SpaceXR — MCP Functional & Contract Specification
Version 1.0 · Draft contract · 6 November 2026
Complete topic and method catalog, JSON Schema parameters, grammar rules, resource surfaces, user experiences and operational semantics. Prepared for implementation with @cyanmycelium/mcp-core.
PART I — MCP CONTRACT
1. Topics / namespaces
Topic

Purpose

10

Operations, permissions, discovery
2. Naming, grammar and type conventions
Canonical MCP tool names use snake_case: namespace_method (e.g. navigation_flyBy). The human-facing conceptual name is namespace.method. This is an authored contract, not an assertion about an existing runtime.
Tool inputs use JSON Schema objects with additionalProperties=false and explicit required keys. ISO timestamps use date-time. Distances are meters, durations seconds, angles degrees unless otherwise stated.
A target descriptor is a tagged object: {kind: "body"|"landmark"|"position"|"object", bodyId?, landmarkId?, position?, objectId?}. A position includes bodyId, latitudeDegrees, longitudeDegrees, altitudeMeters?, coordinateConvention?, datum?.
time="now" evaluates the actual astronomical epoch; time="simulation" uses the currently selected epoch; an ISO instant fixes a historical/future epoch. experience duration is always distinct from astronomical time.
Long-running actions return status="accepted" and operationId. Poll control_getOperation or read spacexr://operation/{operationId}. MCP tasks/progress are not assumed supported by mcp-core.
Every scientific result should expose sourceId, epoch, resolution/coverage, quality and uncertainty when available. Unknown must remain unknown; no synthetic precision.
Mutating actions require an authorized mode. The user can interrupt navigation at any time. Public screens must not expose private mission or user data.

4. Resources and resource templates
spacexr://session/context — Active observer context
spacexr://universe/bodies — Celestial body catalog
spacexr://navigation/current — Active navigation state
spacexr://time/state — Simulation clock
spacexr://tv/state — Ambient mode state
spacexr://missions — Mission index
spacexr://permissions — Current session permissions
spacexr://body/{bodyId} — Celestial body state
spacexr://mission/{missionId} — Mission state
spacexr://operation/{operationId} — Asynchronous operation state
spacexr://scene/object/{objectId} — Scene object state
5. Grammar and mcp-core integration
Behavior: declare MCP tools, inputSchema, outputSchema, resource definitions and templates. Adapter: implement execution, capability filtering and resource-change events. State: return read-only snapshots. Grammar: client/locale wording in McpGrammar.fromJSON compatible files.
The grammar.default.en.json and grammar.default.fr.json files use server, tools, properties and phrases sections. Their descriptions can be loaded as a grammar layer. They are not a replacement for the Behavior schemas.
The namespace catalogs (*.tools.json) are design-time JSON files that must be converted into McpTool[] in _buildTools(). Do not pass these catalogs directly to McpGrammar.fromJSON.
mcp-core currently exposes resource subscriptions and structuredContent; its README lists progress, cancellation and MCP tasks as not yet implemented. SpaceXR operation IDs are therefore an application-level pattern.
Use a broker when multiple servers, a browser tunnel or centralized access control are needed. mcp-core alone suffices for an individual MCP server.
PART II — FUNCTIONAL EXPERIENCES
Continuous interplanetary travel
Leave Earth, travel to the Moon, descend to Shackleton, depart for Mars without a scene-selection screen.
Illustrative tool sequence: universe_findBodies → ephemeris_getState → navigation_preview → navigation_flyTo → navigation_land
Autonomous scientific site comparison
Find three candidate sites near Shackleton, inspect illumination, slope and proximity to candidate resources, present side-by-side views and tradeoffs.
Illustrative tool sequence: surface_findCandidates → surface_compareSites → scene_addMarker → scene_compareViews → time_animateRange
Show me why
When an agent recommends a site, replay a visual explanation with source and uncertainty, and allow immediate interruption.
Illustrative tool sequence: mission_create → mission_addWaypoint → mission_addAction → mission_execute
Historical mission replay
Replay lunar or Martian mission itineraries with contextual annotations and user-controlled time.
Illustrative tool sequence: mission_replay → time_set → navigation_follow
Cosmic scale comparison
Compare Olympus Mons with Everest or a lunar crater with a city using a common visual scale.
Illustrative tool sequence: surface_getProfile → scene_addAnnotation → scene_compareViews
AI copiloting
Guide, copilot and autonomous modes; user can always reclaim control.
Illustrative tool sequence: control_getPermissions → control_setAgentMode → navigation_stop
SpaceXR TV
Use idle displays for endless explorer, orbital window, grand tour or cosmic relax, with no blank/loading screen.
Illustrative tool sequence: tv_start → tv_setPreferences → tv_enqueue → tv_getNowPlaying → tv_nextScene
TV to interactive handoff
A viewer clicks the screen or scans a QR code to open the current location and epoch.
Illustrative tool sequence: tv_getNowPlaying → tv_takeOver → observer_getContext
Shared persistent mission
Save and share itinerary, viewpoints, annotations, assumptions and decisions for replay by another user or agent.
Illustrative tool sequence: mission_save → mission_share → mission_replay
PART III — CONTRACT EXAMPLES AND ACCEPTANCE
flyByAtCurrentTime
{  "name": "navigation_flyByAtCurrentTime",  "arguments": {    "target": {      "kind": "body",      "bodyId": "mars"    },    "durationSeconds": 20,    "closestApproachMeters": 1500000  }}
Compare Shackleton candidates
{  "name": "surface_findCandidates",  "arguments": {    "bodyId": "moon",    "region": {      "kind": "named-region",      "landmarkId": "shackleton"    },    "criteria": {      "maxSlopeDegrees": 8,      "maxResults": 3    },    "maxResults": 3  }}

{  "name": "tv_start",  "arguments": {    "mode": "endless"  }}

{  "name": "observer_getContext",  "arguments": {}}
Acceptance criteria
No missing tiles are deliberately exposed as finished content in TV mode; retain prior shot or choose another.
Every navigation operation can be queried and stopped using an operationId; user input takes precedence.
The agent discovers capabilities before promising a landing or scientific measurement.
A time-fixed flyby is not falsely described as a physically simulated transfer.
Scientific comparisons preserve provenance and uncertainty; an attractive visualization is not scientific proof.
A mission can be saved, replayed, inspected and shared according to permissions.
All JSON files parse, all method names are unique and every declared required parameter exists in properties.
Sources and scope
mcp-core repository: https://github.com/pandaGaume/mcp-core (README reviewed 6 November 2026). This is a proposed SpaceXR interface and must be validated against runtime capabilities before implementation.
